title: Launcher silhouette has weak secondary shape
observed: Current launcher identity is a generic terminal chevron plus a cursor at 45% alpha; raster branding adds glow. Both source assets were visually inspected.
impact: The cursor fades at launcher size, leaving a familiar terminal mark rather than a distinct product identity. Glow creates softness rather than useful detail.
proposal: Replace with the open-portal two-bracket concept; retain its full-alpha silhouette in monochrome.
verification: ImageGen concept preserved; deterministic vector and legacy resources implemented, Android AAPT2 36.1.0 compile passes. Inline AppBrandMark SVG rendered at32px and tested at24px. Circle/squircle/themed previews inspected. No installed-launcher evidence yet. Follow-up bundled app-icon-256.png regenerated from the same vector/background and visually inspected; this also unifies in-app bitmap/Linux window branding. Large marketing raster remains historical.

title: In-app glyphs vary in stroke and subject clarity
observed: Current navigation mixes Material workspace dots, outlined folder/bell and rounded action glyphs. Actual package-font comparison shows Phosphor regular and duotone alternatives.
impact: Different optical weights and abstract workspace dots make the interface feel assembled and weaken recognition of conversations as the main activity.
proposal: Adopt Phosphor regular as the shared action family; duotone selected conversation/folder/bell, regular More, fill Stop. Use semantic AppIconography constants.
verification: Base shared module tested in Flutter 3.47.2 and actual light/dark renders inspected. Official package2.1.0 fails because IconData is final; approved native constants plus exact MIT fonts replace wrapper. Follow-up ba67d91 supplies272-name migration map,252 replacements and20 KEEP states; whole-page adoption and supplementary integration checks belong to coordinator.

title: Adaptive resources must follow the approved identity
observed: Android already uses foreground/background adaptive layers and API33 monochrome; marketing raster is a separately maintained asset.
impact: Changing the attractive raster alone would not change modern Android launchers and could create a split product identity.
proposal: Use deterministic approved vector for adaptive foreground and monochrome, separate full-bleed background and generated legacy mipmaps; verify real launcher masks before claiming installation.
verification: Foreground/monochrome two-path geometry identical, central66dp safe-circle bound checked; five legacy density assets regenerate byte-for-byte. AAPT2 36.1.0 compiles Android res. Installed launcher/theme-mask verification remains pending.

title: New glyph family needs a single semantics and sizing policy
observed: Published Phosphor duotone widget paints two Icon layers and propagates semanticLabel; standard app controls already enforce 48dp targets.
impact: A naive migration risks duplicate announcements and shrinking touch areas to match the lighter glyphs.
proposal: Use native AppGlyph with one optional semantic label;24px main/20px inline glyphs inside48dp targets, no thin/light weights; technical glyphs do not mirror, high contrast omits decorative duotone layer.
verification: Pinned Flutter3.47.2: five module widget tests and two actual-font/SVG render fixtures pass; scoped analyzer clean. Semantic labels once,24px brand layout,20px action in48dp button, high contrast outline, RTL technical orientation verified. AppGlyph uses native Icon layers with one external label. No physical-device touch or TalkBack walkthrough claimed.

title: Delight should respond to intent
observed: Navigation supports a 220ms transition; composer already has continuous activity glow.
impact: Adding bounce or pulse to every new glyph would compete with real task state.
proposal: Use 150–180ms selection fade, unchanged hit target, brief confirmation response; keep normal actions still and progress tied to real work.
verification: Module has no independent animation or perpetual pulse. Selection transition remains owned by navigation/page integration; no FPS or motion-sensitivity validation claimed.
